questions.question: Which package holds the Comparable interface?
questions.explanation: Comparable lives in java.lang, so it needs no import. Comparator lives in java.util.

questions.question: a.compareTo(b) returns -7. What does that tell a sorting method?
questions.explanation: Only the sign matters. Any negative value means a is placed before b.

questions.question: What does this print? System.out.println(Integer.compare(40, 15));
questions.explanation: Integer.compare returns 1 when the first value is larger, -1 when it is smaller and 0 when they match.

questions.question: Bib implements Comparable by time only. What does this print? TreeSet<Bib> t = new TreeSet<>(); t.add(new Bib(7, 300)); t.add(new Bib(9, 300)); System.out.println(t.size());
questions.explanation: Both bibs have time 300, so compareTo returns 0 and the TreeSet treats the second one as a duplicate.

questions.question: compareTo is written as: return this.points - other.points; Why can this sort some values in the wrong order?
options: The difference can overflow int and flip its sign
Fields cannot be read inside compareTo
questions.explanation: For values far apart, such as 2,100,000,000 and -100,000,000, the difference wraps to a negative int.

questions.question: A Parcel class has no compareTo. Why does new TreeSet<Parcel>().add(new Parcel()) fail?
options: add returns false for new objects
TreeSet casts the element to Comparable and throws ClassCastException
questions.explanation: Without a Comparator, TreeSet relies on the natural order, so an element that is not Comparable fails on the first add.

questions.question: What does it mean for compareTo to be consistent with equals?
options: compareTo returns 0 exactly when equals returns true
Both methods must be declared final
questions.explanation: When the zero result and equals agree, sorted collections like TreeSet behave the same way as HashSet would.

questions.question: What does this print? String[] c = {"pear", "Fig", "apple"}; Arrays.sort(c); System.out.println(Arrays.toString(c));
questions.explanation: String's natural order compares character codes, and uppercase F (70) comes before lowercase a (97).

questions.question: You need to sort the same Ticket objects by price on one screen and by date on another. What should you use?
options: One natural order plus Comparator objects for other orders
questions.explanation: A class has one compareTo. Extra orders belong in separate Comparator objects passed to the sort method.

questions.question: Which tool is best for comparing two double fields inside compareTo?
questions.explanation: Casting a small difference such as 0.4 to int gives 0. Double.compare also handles NaN and -0.0 correctly.
